previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 19th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, which was managed with lorazepam and prochlorperazine. Methotrexate levels were monitored daily, declining to 0.14 uM by discharge, allowing safe transition home. Leucovorin rescue and sodium bicarbonate were administered as scheduled to support methotrexate clearance. Aspirin was held during admission and restarted at discharge, with heparin used for DVT prophylaxis. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation, and her hemoglobin remained stable. She reported ongoing chronic right foot pain, managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone, and denied depressive symptoms, remaining on citalopram. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete three days of leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate and to continue alternating methotrexate and rituximab therapy.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ female with h/o primary CNS lymphoma treated with high dose 
methotrexate who is admitted now for cycle 20 of HD MTX. She 
received IV fluids to alkalinize her urine. She was given 
methotrexate from 11pm on ___ to 1am on ___ with urine pH 
>8.5. she received leucovorin rescue starting 24 hours after 
methotrexate. Her methotrexate level at approximately 30 hours 
was 0.17. She received bicarbonate IVF and leucovorin for 
approximately 12 more hours after that point and is being 
discharged with no additional PO leucovorin or bicarbonate.
Of note, she received fosaprepitant prior to chemotherapy 
instead of zofran. This resulted in good control of her nausea 
and none of the headaches she was getting with zofran.
